statement: Foundation Phase intentionally contains no novel experiments; future sessions must preserve this phase boundary until a human supplies Phase 2 authorization.

The primary Comellas-Yebra figure uses (x,0) as its first point, while the protected problems/heilbronn_n12/BASELINE.md says (0,0), creating zero triangle area for points 0,2,8. Source-faithful coordinates reproduce the exact 0.032598858691819698... baseline. Heilbronn search is blocked pending human amendment and a new foundation version.

The pinned evaluator and metric checkout are available at the exact upstream commit, but native Windows multiprocessing cannot re-import its dynamically loaded user_program module. No finite metric result was obtained; do not spend active search compute until a Linux-compatible runtime is available.

Clamping the published scope-112 witness to scope 111 gives a reproducible 100/105 unique-difference state with duplicate set [13,36,53,100,111]. Three 20-second single-mark simulated-annealing seeds did not leave this local basin, so single-mark retuning is not informative without multi-row or multi-mark moves.

From-scratch random Golomb-ruler sampling with 3000 candidates per level repeatedly dead-ended at four mutually disjoint rows after 0.684M-1.017M sampled rows per seed. Greedy irreversible choice is the dominant failure mode; a compatible-pool index and backtracking are needed before further random sampling.

Exhaustive radius-10 first-row replacement against fixed rows 1-6 found no compatible complete row at scope 111. The clamped witness's five conflicts cannot be resolved in that one-row neighborhood; this is local negative evidence only.

Two-mark and whole-row annealing across all seven rows also remained at 100/105 unique differences with duplicate set [13,36,53,100,111] for three seeds. More temperature tuning of this score is not justified without a new representation.

A radius-25 compatibility-pool search consumed each 30-second deadline saturating only 114-133 unique candidates for variable row 0; no other variable-row pools or DFS nodes were reached. Candidate-pool size must be bounded per row and search time allocated across rows.

OR-Tools 9.15.6755 CpSolver.solve crashes with a Windows access violation even on a three-variable AllDifferent control model. The scope-111 CP-SAT model produced no status or bound; this is runtime evidence only and should not be interpreted as infeasibility.

Upstream-inspired reversible block deletion improved pure-Python partial assembly from the prior four-row/60-difference greedy ceiling to five rows/75 unique differences for all three seeds, with 7,182-8,154 replacements per seed. No run completed seven rows or produced a validator-accepted scope-111 witness, so the gain is Level 1 proxy evidence only and active search is paused.

WSL2 Linux OR-Tools 9.15.6755 ran the unchanged exact scope-111 CP-SAT model without the native Windows access violation, but returned UNKNOWN after 120.147 seconds with no candidate or bound. Combined with Windows OR-Tools 9.12 and the tested redundant-propagation variant, the current direct formulation is low-yield for further short repeats; UNKNOWN is not mathematical infeasibility.

The exact pinned k-server taxi evaluator is operational in WSL2 with an external fork-start wrapper. The pinned parametrized example scores 17 violations, matching the upstream README's human-designed baseline; the separately reported 3-violation candidate is not included in the pinned checkout, so evaluator operation is verified but the 3 result is not reproduced.

Z3 5.1.0.0 ran the direct scope-111 integer Distinct model under WSL2 but returned unknown after 120.017 seconds with no candidate or bound. A second exact solver family did not resolve the current monolithic formulation; more direct solver churn is low-value.

Exhaustive radius-3 perturbation pools around all seven published rows contained 48,100 valid row masks. Exact compatibility DFS reached depth 5 before its 5,000,000-node cap, showing coordinated local repair has a larger search space than the one-row test but no complete witness.

Candidate-level CP-SAT exact-cover propagation over the same 48,100 radius-3 row masks returned UNKNOWN after 121.657 seconds with no assignment or bound. The finite neighborhood remains unresolved; this does not justify another short CP-SAT repeat.

A Glucose4 sequential-counter SAT encoding of the radius-3 candidate cover exceeded its 120-second wall budget without returning a status or artifact and was interrupted. The encoding is not a practical short-budget route in its current form; no satisfiability inference is made.

Twelve fixed-orientation SLSQP starts from the source-faithful Comellas-Yebra coordinates returned to the published minimum within float64 noise. No certified improvement or global negative result exists, and the protected transcription remains unusable for official comparison.

A 250,000-row deduplicated uniform catalog of valid scope-111 Golomb rulers, followed by rare-difference exact-cover branching, reached depth 4 before a 2,000,000-node cap. This matches the earlier global-greedy ceiling; uniform catalog expansion is low-value without a structural bias.

The pinned staged n=7 search reached its controller with a startup edge-order proxy in three local configurations: six fast plus three heavy workers caused a confirmed WSL global OOM; one fast plus three heavy workers failed with Wsl/Service/E_UNEXPECTED; one fast plus two heavy workers again made WSL unresponsive before any completed stage result. These runs provide no candidate evidence. Further local concurrency tuning is low-value without a more capable stable runtime or the missing reported 3-violation workspace.

A 100,000-mask library of individually valid scope-111 Golomb rulers did not pack into a complete DTS under either generic best-response swaps (96 unique differences) or explicit duplicate-conflict swaps (97 unique differences). Both states were rejected by the integer verifier. Valid-row library packing is low-yield without a new structural source of compatible masks.

The public FPGA-reference C search, adapted to n=7,k=5,M=111, completed separated training at TRAINING_M=152. Default persistence thresholds reached main search but repeatedly stalled at six rows; increasing the thresholds completed training but consumed the 120-second software budget before any main status. No candidate was decoded. This closes the bounded software reference family without an infeasibility claim; hardware-scale execution or a new structural construction is required.

Three new structured DTS families gave no target witness: affine gap coupling reached 89 unique differences, quadratic gap coupling reached 79, and exhaustive p=43 Ruzsa/Ling residue splitting completed 10,922,688 balanced transforms with best valid scope 195. These tested families should remain closed; this is not evidence of global DTS infeasibility.

For the pinned n=7 k-server Potential, the circle B cache is approximately 1001 x 279936 int32, about 1.12GB per process. The prior multi-worker staged configurations therefore duplicate a large cache and can exhaust the current WSL memory. A single-process/shared-cache architecture is a materially different runtime experiment; it does not change the evaluator or establish a k-server result.

A single-process architecture removed the prior cache-duplication failure: it built the 1001 x 279936 int32 circle cache and completed 700 exact circle candidates, including logged zero-violation circle milestones. However, one sequential full pinned taxi evaluation remained active past 1200 seconds and produced no violations_k score. The remaining bottleneck is full taxi potential evaluation, not worker initialization; further local concurrency tuning is low-value.

A screen that eliminated all five known violations of the independently reproduced 5-violation seed selected coefficient-8 mutations that scored 348,550 violations on the full taxi metric. Fixed-edge repair is therefore not a valid global selector for the canonical potential family; newly introduced violations dominate. Future local search must use a global screen or exact full metric.

The two highest-ranked preserved non-seed zero-circle candidates from the completed circle artifact each scored 54 violations on all 7,000,602 taxi inequalities, versus 5 for the pinned upstream seed. Excluding known seeds repaired provenance selection but did not produce global quality; the same circle-zero top-20 selector is closed under the current evaluator.

The released-cache pipeline completed 686 exact circle candidates and full-scored two finalists in about 442 seconds each, but deterministic tie-breaking selected the first two pinned upstream seed vectors among tied zero-circle candidates. Both returned 5 violations on all 7,000,602 taxi inequalities. Circle zero scores are therefore not sufficient for novelty-preserving selection; future exact gates must exclude every pinned seed and the zero vector before ranking preserved candidates.

The verified 5-violation canonical seed scored zero violations on the complete circle m=6 instance. Adding alpha times the translation-invariant work-function spread produced 240 to 1,794 violations for every tested nonzero alpha, so this nonlinear correction family is not circle-feasible in the tested range and should not consume taxi-scale evaluation budget.

With the verified 5-violation coefficients held fixed, the unchanged five-row index matrix scored 0 on all 6,006 complete-circle inequalities. All 13 row-0 uniform signed-anchor replacements and six global cyclic relabels scored 204 to 1,038 violations, so these natural matrix variations are tightly constrained and closed without taxi-scale evaluation.

Across 49 total deterministic variants (47 non-control row-anchor, global-relabel, one-row cyclic-orbit, and sign-flip index_matrix variants plus the repeated base controls), the unchanged five-row canonical matrix was the only complete-circle-feasible variant around the verified 5-violation seed. The best non-control scored 24 violations; further local matrix tuning is low-value without a new structural mechanism.

Native C++ two-word difference masks did not remove the dominant cost in the tested design: constructing a one-million-row deduplicated random Golomb catalogue consumed the full 360-second wall budget, leaving only 16521 finite DFS nodes and maximum depth 4. The run produced no scope<=111 witness and gives no infeasibility evidence. Any revival must separate or materially accelerate catalogue construction rather than repeat the same in-memory random generator.

A persistent one-million-row random Golomb catalogue generated in 4.37 seconds, but static rare-difference exact-cover branching reached only depth 5 at 1796 nodes in 240 seconds. Replacing the prior dynamic compatibility-count scan did not make the random catalogue tree tractable; further random-catalogue tuning is low-value without a new row-generation or structural decomposition mechanism.

The verified canonical hard-min potential scored 0 on all 6006 complete-circle edges, but normalized entropic soft-min aggregation over the same configuration energies scored 1362 violations at temperatures 0.01 through 0.5 and 1398 to 1476 at temperatures 1 through 16. Independent endpoint evaluation matched these scores; the soft-min family is closed before taxi-scale evaluation.

The explicit published n=5 k=4 candidate is reproducible under the pinned evaluator: 0 violations on the complete circle m=6 control and 3 on the 7,000,602-edge circle-taxi m=6 metric. An independent direct canonical-potential and array-inequality count matched both totals and the three taxi edge indexes. This replaces the local five-violation n=7 seed as the verified finite baseline, but it is prior art and does not reach the strict target below 3.

The verified n=5 prior-art candidate's complete-circle gate admitted 11 of 20 single +/-1 coefficient neighbors, but all 20 regressed on the frozen taxi metric: the best neighbor had 18 violations versus the control's 3. The one-step coefficient neighborhood is therefore closed without strict improvement; complete-circle feasibility did not predict taxi performance locally.

A bounded L1 solve over 16 symmetry-aware pairwise-distance work-function features was infeasible for repairing all three residual taxi failures or any pair while preserving all 6006 complete-circle inequalities. The residual directions are outside this low-dimensional additive correction cone; further tuning of the same feature family is low-value.

All four bounded LP models were infeasible over the full 126 m=6 work-function coordinates: no additive correction could repair even two of the three residual taxi edges while preserving all 6006 complete-circle inequalities. The additive correction family is closed at full coordinate expressivity; future work must alter the min-envelope or use a different nonlinear potential form.

Thirty max/min offset switches between the verified n=5 candidate and three documented canonical alternatives all passed the complete-circle screen, but taxi counts were 3 for 15, 14 for 5, 17 for 5, and 588 for 5. Envelope switching did not repair the residual mechanism; further offset or alternative tuning is low-value.

A direct integer longest-path relaxation produced a 166681-node potential table satisfying all 7000602 frozen taxi inequalities; an independent array audit and the pinned primary evaluator both gave violations_k=0. Only 105 of 1001 complete-circle work-function nodes matched the taxi table, and zero fallback produced 1491 circle violations. This is a strict frozen-evaluator witness but an overfit finite artifact, not a transferable k-server potential or proof.

Exhaustive full-domain replacement of one row around the clamped scope-112 witness found zero compatible scope-111 rows: the only consistent fixed-six case visited 108 nodes with no complete row, while the other six omissions had fixed-set collisions. The radius-10 local result was therefore not hiding a distant one-row repair.

State-conditioned incremental row generation reached six mutually difference-disjoint rows on two of three 60-second seeds, improving the observed depth-five static-catalogue frontier, but no seventh row or scope-111 witness appeared. The six-row partials independently audited to 90 unique differences each; this is methodological Level 1 evidence only.

Replacing sampled sixth/seventh-row branching with exact final-pair enumeration consumed the three declared 60-second budgets without a disjoint pair. Only 8, 4, and 4 compatible terminal rows were found across visited prefixes, with 4, 2, and 6 pair checks; the current state-conditioned prefix policy is not productive at this budget.

Exhaustive fixed-five enumeration around the clamped published witness found six consistent omitted-row pairs, 16 compatible rows, and 20 pair checks, with zero disjoint pairs. A standalone Python implementation reproduced all per-case counts; the witness cannot be repaired by changing two rows.

Exhaustive fixed-four enumeration around the clamped published witness found 16 consistent omitted-row triples, 1,732 compatible rows, and 6,896 triple checks, with zero pairwise-disjoint triples. A standalone Python implementation reproduced the aggregate counts; the published-witness repair basin is closed through three changed rows, without any global infeasibility inference.

A NumPy-only full-coordinate differential-evolution search with three fixed seeds, a retained source-faithful elite, 1,500 generations, and 7,000 Gaussian polish proposals per seed returned to the Comellas--Yebra source-faithful configuration in every run. An independent 100-digit Decimal audit of the retained decimal candidate found all 220 triangles and minimum area 0.032598858691819690, with no strict improvement over the exact baseline. This closes the tested global-DE family at this budget, not Heilbronn optimization in general.

The complete scope-111 DTS decision problem was encoded as a preserved 15540-variable/1461683-clause one-hot CNF. Two materially different CDCL solvers, Kissat 4.0.3 and CaDiCaL 2.1.3, each returned UNKNOWN at a 120-second budget without emitting a model. This closes the tested full-domain SAT encoding/solver portfolio at the current budget as runtime-inconclusive evidence; it does not prove global DTS infeasibility and future work requires a different encoding, stronger capability, or structural construction.

Three fixed-seed native memetic runs combining row-level crossover, valid-row injection, and duplicate-directed coordinate repair converged to the same internally valid 103/105 state, with duplicate differences [10,21]. This is reproducible Level 1 proxy improvement over the clamped 100/105 anchor, but no target witness was produced.

An exhaustive one/two-coordinate audit of the 103/105 memetic state covered 3,885 one-coordinate and 7,330,995 two-coordinate replacements over all 35 nonzero mark positions. Of these, 4,187,558 were internally valid; the maximum remained 103 and both independent integer verifiers rejected the best state for duplicate differences [10,21]. This closes the tested memetic basin through two coordinate changes without implying global DTS infeasibility.

Exact replacement of row 0 in the reproducible 103/105 memetic state against the other six rows visited 108 recursion nodes and found zero compatible six-mark Golomb rows. The fixed six rows occupy 90 unique differences, leaving 21 admissible differences, but none supports a complete replacement row. This closes the full one-row repair basin without implying global DTS infeasibility.

Fixing the four mutually compatible rows 1, 3, 5, and 6 of the memetic 103/105 state produced an exact catalog of 84 compatible Golomb rows. Exhaustive rare-difference packing visited 131 nodes and found no disjoint triple for replacement rows 0, 2, and 4. This closes that fixed-four repair decomposition without implying global DTS infeasibility.

Fixing rows 1, 3, and 5 of the memetic 103/105 state produced an exact catalog of 9,644 compatible Golomb rows. Exhaustive rare-difference packing visited 180,037 nodes, reached no disjoint quadruple, and did not time out. Thus the tested four-row repair class changing rows 0, 2, 4, and 6 is closed, but global DTS infeasibility remains unproved.
